title: Working Out the Money Put Back for a Dental, Vision or Hearing Cost Met Elsewhere
content:
This is the accounting basis on which the money put back onto a Ridgecrest Healthy Options Card is worked out where another payer has since met a dental, vision or hearing cost the card had already paid.

**The quantity.** The money put back is what the card has been charged at dental, vision and hearing providers in the stretch of the card's own record that is looked at, worked out on the basis the card's tier gives, and never more than what the card was charged at those providers; it is rounded to the nearest cent at the end and at no earlier step. It is never less than nothing.

**The quantities it is built from.**

1. *The stretch looked at.* The stretch looked at is the whole of the benefit year to date, that is the 12 months of the benefit year up to the day the money going back is worked out.
2. *What the card has been charged at those providers.* What the card has been charged at those providers is the total of every transaction posted at them in that stretch, whatever became of it.
3. *What another payer has met.* What another payer has met is taken as nothing.
4. *What the member was left to bear.* What the member was left to bear is taken as nothing.
5. *The money going back.* The money going back is taken as the whole of what the card was charged at those providers.

**Where it is placed.** It is placed in the benefit period the transaction it relates to belonged to, so that money coming back near the end of a period does not quietly become a fresh allowance.

**Worked through on hypothetical figures.** Take a card whose entries at dental, vision and hearing providers in the benefit year to date come to 61.40 USD, 128.15 USD and 40.00 USD. What the card has been charged at those providers is the total of the three, 229.55 USD. What another payer has met is nothing and what the member was left to bear is nothing, so the money going back is the whole 229.55 USD. That figure is not more than what the card was charged at those providers, and it is not less than nothing, so the money put back is 229.55 USD, rounded to the nearest cent once at the end. It is placed in the benefit period the transaction it relates to belonged to.
